caption: This drawing depicts a single silver teapot viewed from the side against a plain background. The teapot has a round, bulbous body and sits on a short, circular pedestal base. It features an elongated, curved spout on the left and a large, ornate handle on the right, with a small scroll at the top of the handle. The teapot has a domed lid with a pineapple-shaped finial. Decorative embellishments are visible along the top edge near the lid and around the finial. There appears to be a script letter, possibly an “L,” engraved on the side of the teapot’s body. The drawing is rendered in shades of gray pencil on aged, brownish paper, with visible smudges and minor stains around the edges. The words “SILVER TEAPOT” are written above the teapot in capital letters, and there are additional handwritten notes below the teapot, including dimensions and the artist’s name, “JOHN GRAY,” along with further notes related to a museum case and catalog number.
title: Silver Teapot
cluster: #19 — Ceramic Arts: Pottery, Stoneware, and Porcelain
